Meta’s reproducible [HSTU configuration](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/configs/ml-1m/hstu-sampled-softmax-n128-final.gin) uses 128 negatives, temperature 0.05, and L2-normalized query/item embeddings. Its [local sampler](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/generative_recommenders/research/modeling/sequential/autoregressive_losses.py) draws uniform negatives independently **per supervised position**, with replacement—not one shared batch pool. Negative duplicates remain; the [loss](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/generative_recommenders/research/modeling/sequential/losses/sampled_softmax.py) masks target collisions and applies uncorrected sampled cross-entropy. These sources do not establish an implemented comparison against a text-neighbor curriculum.

A concrete proposed ablation: retain the corrected HSTU backbone, temperature 0.05, seeds 0/42, 200-epoch maximum and 200 batches/epoch. Compare 128 uniform negatives against uniform sampling for epochs 1–20, then linearly increase the text-neighbor sampling probability to 0.25 across epochs 21–60; hold thereafter. Build deterministic top-100 cosine neighbors using TF-IDF over supplied titles/descriptions, without pretrained models. At each position, repeatedly choose uniform or neighbor sampling, rejecting padding, target, observed training-history items and already selected negatives; use uniform fallback for empty neighbor lists. Apply identical filtering/uniqueness to the uniform control. This is a proposed experiment, not a published result. Text neighbors risk being unobserved positives. Both variants cost O(P·128·d) scoring; neighbor construction adds preprocessing/storage. Shared pools reduce embedding-gather costs but change sampling correlations.

Proposal correction is justified when approximating a specified full-softmax objective. User filtering renormalizes proposals; weighted sampling without replacement requires actual inclusion probabilities, not naïve −log(128q). For an explicit-positive partition estimator, weight negative exponentials by inverse inclusion probability and retain the positive exactly; finite-sample log-loss bias remains. Otherwise, document an uncorrected contrastive objective. [Candidate-sampling definitions](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf), [positive-handling analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331).
